title: Midterm Result Turns Long-Running AI Funding Worries Into a Policy Question
summary:
Technology shares suffered their sharpest one-day fall in months after Democratic gains in the US midterm elections, with the Nasdaq 100 down **6.3%** on Thursday. Investors are weighing what a changed Congress could mean for AI regulation and data-centre expansion.

The election was the trigger rather than the cause. Doubts over whether record AI spending can be financed and repaid had been building for weeks.
context:
- Hyperscalers have guided to extraordinary capital spending this year, and one of them recently reported negative free cash flow. That left the sector exposed to any new threat to the funding story.

- Investors fear tighter oversight, planning limits on data centres or less favourable tax treatment. No specific legislation has been proposed, so the move reflects uncertainty about direction rather than a known policy change.

- The selloff erased roughly **$2.3tn** of market value and spread to Asian AI-linked shares. A partial rebound on Friday suggests some investors see the reaction as overdone.

title: Oil Posts Steepest Weekly Fall Since 2020 as Investors Price In a Possible Iran Settlement
summary:
Brent crude fell by roughly **16%** over the week, its biggest weekly drop since the pandemic, as traders bet that the US midterm results improve the odds of diplomacy with Iran. Prices had carried a large risk premium since the conflict disrupted Gulf shipping earlier this year.

No deal has been signed, so the move reflects expectations rather than any restored supply.
context:
- The war premium dates from the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint for a large share of the world's seaborne crude. Prices rose sharply because traders feared lasting supply loss.

- Analysts stress the fall is a bet on diplomacy. Tanker attacks in the Gulf continued during the week and prompted a partial bounce, so the market remains highly sensitive to headlines.

- Central banks have raised rates because of energy-driven inflation, and lower oil could ease that pressure. Policymakers have said they will wait for evidence the fall lasts before changing course.

title: Bank of England Raises Rates for the First Time Since 2023 on Energy-Led Inflation
summary:
The Bank of England lifted Bank Rate by a quarter-point to **4%**, voting 8–1, in its first increase since August 2023. Governor Andrew Bailey blamed energy costs feeding through into prices, and signalled that further tightening may be needed unless the Middle East conflict eases.

It joins other central banks that are tightening again after expecting to cut.
context:
- UK inflation reached **3.5%** in September, well above the 2% target. The Bank projects it could approach 5% by the middle of next year, because household energy bills are set to rise in January.

- Catherine Mann was the lone dissenter and wanted a half-point rise. Bailey said the hike should not be read as the start of a long run of increases.

- Bailey said the week's fall in energy prices would not have changed this decision, but could affect whether a second hike is needed. Oil's path now matters directly to the December meeting.
